plan: My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $25 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more to me than what others bid. If I win, I'll pay less than my valuation. If I lose, I miss out on potential profit. With no previous round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid seems most rational.

My private value is $31. To maximize profit, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll bid strategically near my value. A bid slightly below my value ($30) allows potential profit if others bid lower. This protects against overpaying while still giving a good chance of winning. I'll aim to pay less than my value, creating a potential profit margin.

My private value is $9. Since I only gain if I win and pay less than my value, I want to bid strategically. With no previous round history, I'll bid close to my value but slightly under. A bid of $8.5 allows me potential profit if I win with a lower second-highest bid. This balanced approach protects my downside while giving a reasonable chance of winning and profiting.
